newsitem.title: UK: Dollar ends steady in Europe but undertone firm.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends steady in Europe but undertone firm.

text.p: The dollar ended the European session quietly steady as the market wound down for the New Year holiday break.
Volume was extremely light and an even quieter day is expected tomorrow with Japan and some European centres, including Germany, on holiday for the New Year break.

Dollar/yen continued firm but was shy of its near 45-month peak of 116.20 reached in New York on Friday. Fragile Japanese asset markets are keeping the yen under pressure with investors worried about Japan's ability to sustain any economic recovery when tax rises start to have an impact.

Thoughts of a near-term Japanese monetary tightening have been put on the back-burner as it seems impossible to tighten both fiscal and monetary policy at a time when the economy is at best only showing patchy signs of recovery.
At 1600 GMT the dollar was at 115.80/85 against Friday's European close of 115.30/43.

Technical analysts were looking for dollar/yen to consolidate around current levels before another test of the upside. They said a dip back to the 115.50-60 area is possible before another break higher and only a dip below crucial support around 114.40 would confirm a medium term trend reversal.
On the mark the dollar was still rangebound at a late 1.5567/74 versus Friday's 1.5557/64.
Today's U.S. economic data had little or no impact with November leading indicators up 0.1 percent after unchanged in October and existing home sales up 1.8 percent in the same month.
While dollar/yen was the main focus, dollar/Swiss enjoyed some attention as it got to its highest level since July 1994.
At 1615 GMT dollar/Swiss stood at 1.3502/12 against 1.3479/89 in late Europe on Friday. It touched a peak of 1.3536 earlier.
Sterling rose to a new four-year high against the yen due to the overall bearishness over the Japanese currency. It was at 195.80/92 yen against a high of 196.19 hit earlier in the day.
